observation: Parent NaFadeNet+ExtrapGate(s=50), 3-split val MAPE 0.1087 ± 0.0085. All capacity what-if rules are already satisfied (P0/P0c/P4b shift predictions by -13 to -70 cycles, 0 violations > 1e-3 cycles); P2 closed (model insensitive to voltage level). Remaining weakness: short-prefix error (prefix 1-10 MAPE 0.12-0.19) and prediction drift across prefixes of the same cell: held-out mean |f(x) - f(truncated x)| / EOL = 0.026 / 0.034 / 0.056 (splits 2021/42/2024), per-cell prediction std across prefixes 6-8% of EOL, although the label (EOL) is identical for every prefix of a cell.
primary_hypothesis: The registered temporal-invariance loss prefix-drift (loss.md §4.2: |f(x) - f(x_trunc)| for a random shorter view of the same sample, x_trunc keeps cycles < j, j = floor(u*i), u ~ U(0.5, 1)), computed on a dropout-free network for both views and balanced by gradients (rho 0.5), lowers the held-out relative drift by >= 50% without making val MAPE worse, and reduces short-prefix error.
question_inherited: After the physics what-if rules proved redundant for the parent, does the registered prefix-consistency invariant improve it?
unresolved_from_reference: Prediction drift across prefixes; short-prefix error.
why_this_experiment: User 2026-11-08 chose prefix-drift (loss.md §4.2, registered) after P2 was closed and P0/P0c/P4 were shown already satisfied. Pre-check: the parent's drift is a measurable 2.6-5.6% of EOL (P2's what-if moved predictions only ~0.002 cycles).
modification: Loss = Relative Huber(0.15) + lambda * L_drift, L_drift = mean |f(x_trunc) - f(x)| (standardised units; both views get gradients, as in the symmetric §4.2 definition), both views computed with dropout disabled (physics_dropout_matched); lambda = 0.5 * median grad-norm ratio on 3 fixed training batches (§5.2). Unit checks: identity view gives drift 0.000 when matched (0.125 with independent dropout masks); finite grads; dropout restored.
held_constant_components: NA-E009 model and config, split 2021, seed 2021, Relative Huber 0.15, Adam 5e-5, batch 128, max 100 / min 5 epochs, patience 5, checkpoint rule, data, masks.
controlled_variables: Split 2021 and training seed 2021, minimum 5 / maximum 100 epochs, patience 5 after epoch 5, diagnostics every 50 steps.
expected_evidence: Split-2021 MAPE/RMSE/Acc@15 vs NA-E009 (0.0999 / 22.5 / 0.743); prefix-band MAPE (esp. 1-10); held-out relative drift (eval mode, same truncation RNG) vs parent 0.026; balance band R median in [0.05, 2.0], active fraction, cosine.
rejection_condition: DISCARD if split-2021 MAPE > 0.1049, or BALANCE_FAIL, or the held-out relative drift does not fall by >= 50% vs NA-E009 (0.026), or the 76-100 prefix-band MAPE regresses by > 0.01 vs NA-E009 (0.1085). Drift metric = tools/posthoc_drift.py on best_checkpoint (eval mode, Generator seed 0, |f(x)-f(x_trunc)|*scale/raw_eol), not the in-run diagnostic. Otherwise confirm on 42/2024 and judge the 3-split mean.
minimum_evidence_requirements: At least five complete epochs; finite MAPE, Acc@15, MAE, and RMSE from one checkpoint; sample and unique-cell counts for every domain; gradient, update, activation, prediction, mask, and compute diagnostics.
required_diagnostics: Epoch learning curve; selected and minimum-MAPE epochs; NaFadeNet block gradients and updates; activation health; prediction spread and bias; prefix, domain, and EOL errors; domain guardrail flags; padding sensitivity; parameters, memory, time, and throughput.
